title: iOS Burst: commit the explicit disable (reproducibility) + macOS player build to re-enable (perf)
summary: M0-UNITY-01 review finding. Burst (com.unity.burst, transitive via URP / Input System / Animation Rigging) is disabled for the iOS build so the Linux game-ci export succeeds (iOS Burst AOT cannot cross-compile from Linux). Two gaps: (1) the disable is NOT committed — no ProjectSettings/BurstAotSettings_iOS.json and no CI flag — so 'Burst off' is not reproducible from a fresh checkout (SECURITY_CHECKLIST §7.1 reproducible builds); (2) Burst is a performance optimizer, so shipping with it off leaves CPU-side performance (Jobs / hot numeric loops in movement, physics, scene-graph math) on the table for device fps. Not a correctness issue and not blocking M0/M1 — the iOS splat render is GPU-sort-bound, so the M1-UNITY-01 render measurement is unaffected. Fix: make the iOS Burst state explicit + committed, and add a macOS Unity player-build lane (Burst AOT compiles arm64 natively on macOS) for perf/TestFlight builds before device perf testing.

acceptance_tests.test: The iOS Burst state is explicit and committed (ProjectSettings/BurstAotSettings_iOS.json or set in ProjectSetup.cs), so a fresh checkout reproduces the same Burst behavior; an EditMode test or a CI note records it.

A macOS Unity player-build lane produces an iOS build with Burst AOT enabled (compiles arm64 natively on macOS), used for perf/TestFlight builds; the Linux export lane stays for fast compile-check CI.
acceptance_tests.evidence: green macOS build log showing Burst enabled

acceptance_tests.test: Device fps is compared Burst-off vs Burst-on on a CPU-bound scene to quantify the gain and confirm the 30 fps target holds with Burst on. Measurements are suggested evidence (SPEC §11), not a gate.

history.event: Created by the Coordinator from the M0-UNITY-01 review (Owner flagged Burst-off + graphics=automatic). Graphics=automatic resolves to Metal-only and is correctly guarded by an EditMode test (ProjectSettingsSmokeTests) — no action needed there. Burst-off is the correct workaround for the Linux iOS export; tracked here for reproducibility + perf.
